clue.text: Freely opt in earnest for formal introduction

indicators.note: done freely, the letters of the three words are not held to their order and are rearranged at will

explanation.surface: Someone casually chooses to be serious about a formal introduction, as if signing up earnestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freely' rearranges OPT IN EARNEST, all twelve letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentation is the act of formally introducing someone, as at court or to an audience.

clue.text: Father's wise transaction

parts.note: father is PA, and the possessive adds S
a wise person is sage; sage is also an adjective meaning wise

explanation.surface: A shrewd deal made by Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of 'Father's' supplies the S that joins PA to SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Passage is an older word for a transaction or exchange, as in a passage of arms or words between parties.

clue.text: Was left sheltering son

indicators.note: one word shelters another by holding it inside, as a roof covers someone

parts.note: to have left a place is to have exited it

explanation.surface: Someone departed, protecting their boy as they went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' looks like a mere auxiliary verb opening the sentence, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, so the past tense of being, was, matches having existed.

clue.text: Puts into practice duties surrounding English king

indicators.note: the taxes word goes around the other pieces, so it surrounds them

parts.note: excises are duties, taxes charged on goods
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Taxes levied around an English monarch are actually being applied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duties' here means taxes, not obligations; 'surrounding' wraps them around ER, the English king.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to use it, putting it into practice.

clue.text: Lots circling western urban areas

indicators.note: the larger word runs round the letter like a ring, enclosing it

parts.note: tons is informal for lots, a great quantity

explanation.surface: Many places dotted around the West are built-up districts.
explanation.definitionFit: Towns are settlements larger than villages, the built-up urban areas of a region.

clue.text: Second Police Sergeant providing muscle

parts.note: a trice is an instant, a second

explanation.surface: A second police sergeant brings the brawn to the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal describing the sergeant; it is a noun meaning a moment. 'Providing' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: Dismissed team? Unlikely

parts.note: in cricket a dismissed batsman is out
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A team that has been bowled out? It seems improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batting team is dismissed when it is all out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outside chance is a remote one, so the adjective means unlikely to happen.

clue.text: Public notice determines VAT wrongly

indicators.note: letters put down wrongly are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A published notice sets value added tax incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' rearranges DETERMINES VAT. VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertisement is an announcement put before the public, such as a notice in a newspaper.

clue.text: Making sense of redundant sign being moved

indicators.note: letters being moved around are shifted out of their order into a new one

explanation.surface: Someone figures out why a road sign no longer needed is being relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being moved' rearranges REDUNDANT SIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Understanding a thing is grasping it, comprehending or making sense of what it means.

clue.text: Undeterred by spume in Welsh river

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: the Dee rises in Wales and flows into England
spume is foam or spray, as is spit

explanation.surface: A swimmer presses on regardless of the froth in a river in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Dee rises in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Despite something means in spite of it, carrying on undeterred by it.

clue.text: Court order cardinal put on paper

parts.note: a writ is a formal legal document issued by a court, ordering an action
ten is a cardinal number, a counting number

explanation.surface: A churchman has been served a court order, now committed to paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a church dignitary; it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Something written has been set down in ink on a page.

clue.text: Stretchy laciest pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, poor, so the word is badly arranged

explanation.surface: The laciest underwear is stretchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear, and is a noun in the surface; it is British slang for rubbish, rearranging LACIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material can be stretched and spring back to shape.

clue.text: Fruitless steps to hide hesitation

indicators.note: the outer word hides the other by covering it inside itself

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for crossing a fence or wall
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Steps taken to conceal one's pausing are unproductive.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is a set of steps over a fence in the British countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile land or effort produces nothing; it is barren or fruitless.

clue.text: General tendency to tear to pieces after tantrum, essentially

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer
the essence of a word is its core, the central letter

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart violently

explanation.surface: Throwing a fit and ripping things apart is generally how it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes the middle letter T of TANTRUM; 'after' places REND after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general direction in which things are moving or developing.

clue.text: Seems upset with short short periods of learning

indicators.note: letters upset are knocked over and come back in a new order
cut short, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: terse means short, curt

explanation.surface: Brief study terms seem to have put someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges SEEMS into SEMES; the first 'short' is TERSE and the second cuts its last letter, leaving TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year term in which a school or university teaches its courses.

clue.text: Update sermon I'd reworked twice in the end

indicators.note: a text that is reworked is reshaped, its letters reordered
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A preacher revises the sermon twice before it is finally modernised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reworked' rearranges SERMON ID into MODERNIS; 'in the end' takes E, the last letter of 'twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: To modernise something is to bring it up to date, adapting it to current ways.

clue.text: Small old city highly valued we hear, struck with wonder

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so a word that sounds like another is wanted

parts.note: prized means highly valued

explanation.surface: An ancient little town, treasured by visitors, leaves them amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' turns PRIZED into its sound-alike PRISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surprised is to be astonished, taken aback by something unexpected.

clue.text: Understand increase of price involving brewed ale

indicators.note: the outer word involves the other by taking it in

parts.note: a rise is an increase, as in a price rise

indicators.note: brewed means mixed up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Grasp why beer prices went up once the ale was brewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' scrambles the ale, and 'involving' sets the result inside the price increase.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become aware of it, grasping it clearly.

clue.text: Regular performance of marsupial and adolescent for the audience

indicators.note: what is for an audience is heard, so the answer sounds like the words

parts.note: a roo is a kangaroo, a marsupial, and a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: A kangaroo and a teenager put on their usual act for spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the audience' signals that ROO plus TEEN, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a set act performed regularly, such as a comedian's or dancer's routine.

clue.text: Drink with some Acapulco coastguards

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A beverage shared with Mexican coastguards in Acapulco.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate drink made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: Too much stored in prison house

indicators.note: the piece is stored in another, kept inside it

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison
OTT is short for over the top, too much

explanation.surface: Far too much is stockpiled in the jail.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT means over the top, excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, typically in the country.

clue.text: Conveys vehicle on trailer not oddly singular

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: not the odd letters, so the even ones are kept

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A vehicle hauls a trailer that is, unusually, not odd and quite unique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not oddly' keeps the even letters of TRAILER, RIE. In a down clue 'on' puts CAR above them.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry something is to transport it, conveying it from place to place.

clue.text: Empty marquee a certain size

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A vacant tent of a definite size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves ME, the outer letters of MARQUEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is a quantity or size, as in a measure of spirits.

clue.text: Boat crew's condition of being tall originally ignored

indicators.note: the original, first letter of the word is ignored, so it is dropped

parts.note: height is the quality of being tall

explanation.surface: A rowing crew's tall stature is overlooked at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally ignored' drops the first letter of HEIGHT. The 's of 'crew's' is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a rowing boat for eight oarsmen, and by extension its crew.

clue.text: About to become weary, daughter went to bed

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to tire is to become weary

explanation.surface: Around the time she grew tired, the girl went off to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to go to bed for the night, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Pinning down any number in poor health

parts.note: N is the mathematician's symbol for any number
ailing means unwell, in poor health

explanation.surface: Diagnosing just how many people are unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing a fact is establishing it firmly, fixing it down as with a nail.

clue.text: One revised a Latin language

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a text revised is reworked, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Someone reworked a Latin text into a different tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' rearranges A LATIN into TALIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is the Romance tongue spoken in Italy, descended from Latin.

clue.text: Still calm about reconstruction of shelters

indicators.note: turned about, the word faces the other way and is read backwards

parts.note: even means calm, as in an even temper

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds these letters in a new order

explanation.surface: The rebuilding of refuges goes on calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns EVEN into NEVE; 'reconstruction of' rearranges SHELTERS into RTHELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, as an adverb, means even so, however: the same as nevertheless.
